decisions.rationale: Evans supplies chronology and textual-overlap arguments, but he also uses the mainstream status of his dating and the outlier status of the alternative as material reasons for dismissal without presenting the relevant scholarly evidence. That reliance on disciplinary status fits the definition.
decisions.context: Evans partly dismisses Luke’s proposed dependence on Josephus by calling his own dating mainstream and characterizing a later date for Luke as an outlier position.

decisions.rationale: Carrier’s stated conclusion is that the notices cannot serve as independent corroboration when their independence cannot be established. Because corroboration requires a warranted independent source, this is an evidentiary limitation rather than treating dependence as true merely because independence has not been proved.

Carrier attempted to construct and apply a background reference class. The summarized weakness is that its membership and comparisons were insufficiently established, not that he underweighted an established base rate in favor of a vivid particular case.

Moving from compatibility to comparative probability is an inferential overreach, but the source does not show Carrier evaluating the inference according to whether its conclusion felt believable. Argument from ignorance more precisely captures the identified defect.

Carrier repeatedly converted the failure of Pauline language to exclude a physical cosmic Jesus into comparative support for that model. Mere compatibility or non-refutation supplies possibility, not positive evidence of probability.
decisions.context: Carrier treats the compatibility of Pauline language with a physical cosmic Jesus as comparative support, although the cited readings principally show that the model is not ruled out.

decisions.rationale: The summarized mechanism interprets disparate sources and speculative motives through Carrier’s preferred fiction-and-literalization account while insufficiently testing the competing remembered-founder explanation. This selective calibration toward an existing theory fits confirmation bias.
decisions.context: Carrier synthesizes initiated insiders, deceived public readers, authorial invention, and later literalization across disparate sources while giving insufficient consideration to competing historical explanations.

decisions.rationale: Comparisons with Holocaust and lunar-landing denial redirect attention from Carrier’s probabilistic historical case to emotionally charged, evidentially disanalogous positions. They supply no Jesus-specific evidence and leave the underlying challenge unanswered.
decisions.context: Evans diverts from Carrier’s probabilistic case by comparing mythicism with Holocaust and lunar-landing denial without adding evidence concerning Jesus’s historicity.

decisions.rationale: Evans treats an archaeologically accurate setting as making fictional composition unusually implausible while overlooking the ordinary background occurrence of historically situated fiction. The ignored reference class directly bears on whether accurate setting supports the protagonist’s existence.
decisions.context: Evans infers that archaeological accuracy makes invention of Jesus unlikely while overlooking the background prevalence of fiction set within accurately represented historical environments.

decisions.rationale: Although Evans relies on the perceived oddity of accurate fictional composition, the more exact defect is his failure to account for the background prevalence of historically situated fiction. Accepting belief bias as well would duplicate the base-rate-neglect label for the same inference.

The summarized replies rely materially on specialist consensus and secondhand rejection without reconstructing the comparative evidence or reasons supporting those judgments. The authorities’ status consequently substitutes for the argument needed to answer Carrier’s cases.
decisions.context: Evans’s comparative-religion replies invoke specialist consensus and secondhand rejection without presenting the underlying evidence or controlled comparisons.

decisions.rationale: Evans asserts and under-defends an earthly interpretation of disputed Pauline markers, but he also identifies textual particulars and offers a cumulative natural-reading inference. Calling those items historical is a contested conclusion and insufficiently supported bridge, not proof that the conclusion was circularly assumed as a premise.

The claimed eyewitness status of the pillars is asserted rather than established by the fellowship episode, so the proposed authority check is under-supported. A contested premise—even one essential to the inference—does not by itself demonstrate that the conclusion was smuggled into the premises.
